source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Stopping today is appropriate because prescribed benzodiazepine use does not produce clinically important physical dependence.","B":"Take a double dose every other day for one week and then stop because intermittent high doses prevent withdrawal more safely than a taper.","C":"Do not stop abruptly; continued benzodiazepine use can cause physical dependence, and dose reduction should follow a gradual patient-specific taper.","D":"Continue the current dose indefinitely because any attempt to taper a benzodiazepine is more dangerous than remaining on long-term therapy."}}
source_row.rationale: Current alprazolam labeling warns that continued benzodiazepine use can produce physical dependence and that abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction can precipitate acute, potentially life-threatening withdrawal. Option C accurately directs a gradual individualized taper. Option A denies dependence risk, Option B invents an unsafe regimen, and Option D incorrectly treats all tapering as contraindicated.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed Alprazolam Tablets — Dosage and Administration §2.3 Discontinuation or Dosage Reduction; Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Dependence and Withdrawal Reactions: continued use can produce physical dependence; abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction may precipitate acute, potentially life-threatening withdrawal; use a gradual patient-specific taper. source_row.stem: A client has taken alprazolam every day for several months and says, “I feel well, so I’m stopping it today.” Which teaching is most important?
